_comment: Per-document invariant exemptions for the ACTS lane.  Same contract as
rules.json: an invariant listed here still RUNS, and its failures are still
counted and printed -- they just do not fail the build for the one document
named in `applies_to`.  Everything else on the lane still gates.
`applies_to` is a substring of metadata.filename, the same scoping rule cases
use.  `invariant` must name an entry in the lane's ALL_INVARIANTS.
Every entry below was traced to its source PDF before being written.  The bar
for adding one is that the invariant is RIGHT and the document is genuinely
outside what the pipeline can read today -- never that a check is
inconvenient.  If an exemption's invariant starts passing, the suite says so
This file did not exist until 2026-09-14.  Round 15 predicted it would be
needed for section_codes_ordered and it was not -- that class was closed by a
parser fix instead.  These three entries are the first acts-lane exemptions.

exemptions.reason: Two heading-only leaves, ss.181 and 189, each traced to the SOURCE MISPRINTING THE SECTION CODE IN THE BODY. The invariant is right: the body text really is in the preceding leaf. (1) Section 181, PDF page 185, prints its body heading as '35.' -- '35. Option to pay fine in lieu of confiscated goods.- Whenever an order for the confiscation of goods is passed under this Act' -- at 12.00pt, x0 93.6, the same size and left margin every other section heading uses. Its contents row on page 3 of the PDF reads '181. Option to pay fine in lieu of confiscated goods. 161'. (2) Section 189, PDF page 191, prints '37. Notice of conviction to be displayed.- (1) Upon the conviction of any person', also 12.00pt at x0 93.6, against a contents row reading '189. Notice of conviction to be displayed. 167'. The neighbours are unaffected: s.180 prints '180.', s.182 prints '182.', s.188 prints '188.' and s.190 prints '190.', so this is not a systematic offset that could be corrected arithmetically -- it is three isolated wrong numbers. THE DEFECT IS THREE SECTIONS WIDE, NOT TWO: s.185D prints '36. In respect of a case transferred to a Special Judge under sub-section(1)' on page 189, and NO INVARIANT CURRENTLY REPORTS IT, because that leaf did pick up a body. A future reader should not conclude from this entry's two hits that the misprint is limited to them. Neither can be read without making the parser wrong about correct documents: the body offers a plausible, well-formed section code that is simply a different number, so the only route is to adopt the contents-page code whenever a body code breaks monotonic order and the heading text matches -- which is exactly the shape rounds 23 and 25 shipped and had to be guarded in round 27, after one of them collapsed 860 of 1,102 rules to stubs in another lane. NO EXPIRY. metadata.source_kind is 'native-digital', so this is not an OCR artifact and nothing about the OCR decision can clear it.

One heading-only leaf, s.26, on an OCR-CLASS DOCUMENT THAT CANNOT BE RE-MEASURED. metadata.source_kind is 'scanned-ocr' and metadata.pipeline_revision is null: this is one of the 14 documents the round-27 re-conversion deliberately skipped, so its output was written by an older parser than the one in the tree. The OCR'd text layer emits the heading terminator GLUED INTO A SINGLE TOKEN -- PDF page 12 prints 'system.—The' as one 9.00pt word, codepoints 0x73 0x79 0x73 0x74 0x65 0x6d 0x2e 0x2014 0x54 0x68 0x65 -- so the heading swallowed the whole body: '26. Commitment control system.—The Finance Division in consultation with the Auditor General shall approve and issue guidelines related to annual and multi-annual commitment control systems.' BE CLEAR ABOUT WHAT THIS ENTRY DOES AND DOES NOT CLAIM: builder.DASHES already contains U+2014, so the CURRENT parser may well read this line correctly and this hit may be nothing more than stale-revision drift. That cannot be tested, because re-converting this document re-runs OCR and data/ocr_cache must stay at 0 B under the decision of record (2026-09-04). This entry exists because 'tracked and deferred' is not a state this suite allows, not because the parser is known to be wrong. EXPIRY: the OCR decision. The day OCR is taken in scope, re-convert this document FIRST and delete this entry if the hit clears.

Two heading-only leaves, ss.27 and 28, which are NOT SECTIONS OF THE ACT AT ALL -- they are rows of its Schedule, on an OCR-class document that cannot be re-measured. metadata.source_kind is 'scanned-ocr' and metadata.pipeline_revision is null, so this is one of the 14 documents round 27 skipped. The Act's Schedule is a two-column table, 'S. No. | Organization / Department / Ministry', introduced on the PDF page carrying '[SCHEDULE]' and '(see sections 2 (n) and 19}'. Its serial-number column is read as section codes, so the output carries 'section 27: Ministry of Defence' and 'section 28: Ministry of Defence Production', each a single line and therefore heading-only, while 'section 29' swallows the remainder of the list ('29. - Ministry of Foreign Affairs\n30. Ministry of Interior\n31. Ministry of National Health Services...'). The parse's own shape is the proof: it emits ONE chapter, 'PART I', whose section codes run 3..23 and then jump straight to 27, 28, 29 -- ss.24, 25 and 26 are absent -- and it emits ZERO schedules. The OCR text layer of that table is visibly degraded and gives the reader nothing to discriminate on: the same serial column prints 'I.' for 1, 'I D.' for 10, '1I.' for 11, '1$.' for 18 and '23,' for 23, alongside 'Ministry of Foreign AffairS', "Terminal'Operators" and a running head reading 'PART q'. A serial column that cannot be told from a section code is not a parser problem that a pattern can fix on this text layer. EXPIRY: the OCR decision. If OCR is ever taken in scope, this document needs re-conversion and a schedule-detection trace before this entry is deleted -- and the right fix then is almost certainly to recover the Schedule as a schedule, not to patch the two leaves this entry names.

exemptions.applies_to: The Sales Tax Act, 1990 amended up to July 01, 2014
exemptions.reason: One heading-only leaf, s.10, where TWO independent defects in the same edition close every route the parser has. (1) THE BODY. PDF page 37 prints the section start as a 7.00pt marker '1' followed by the 12.00pt token '[(10)' -- the code is parenthesised AND wrapped in an amendment bracket -- then 'Refund of input tax.' and TWO separate U+2013 EN DASH tokens. builder._BRACKETPAREN_RE refuses a parenthesised code that carries no letter suffix, and that refusal is LOAD-BEARING, not an oversight: its own comment records that admitting bare CODE made '2 [ (5) The Federal Government may, by notification...' on page 40 of the 2007 edition read as section 5, which advanced the monotonic cursor past pages 32-38 and blocked THIRTY later sections into heading-only stubs. Measured at this commit, the corpus carries 2,505 lines of the shape '[(NN)' across the acts and rules lanes, and they are overwhelmingly inserted SUBSECTIONS ('6[(2) Unless the Board in any case otherwise directs...') or definition clauses. Gating the widening on a heading dash does not separate them: 83 of those lines carry one, and they are s.2 definition clauses -- '3[(3) “associates (associated persons)” means, –', '5[(21) “person” means,–', '1[(44) “time of supply”, in relation to,–' -- so a dash-gated rule would mint 83 phantom sections inside section 2 to recover one real one. (2) THE CONTENTS PAGE. The remaining discriminator would be the contents row, which lists section 10 as expected and unstarted. It cannot be used, because PDF page 3 has NO ToUnicode mapping for the letter 'e': pdfplumber emits the row as 'R(cid:2)fund of input tax' (and 'not(cid:2)' for 'note' on the same page), so the body title 'Refund of input tax' matches nothing. That cid is also why this leaf's heading reads 'R(cid:2)fund of input tax'; per the convention set by rounds 21-28, a source defect is preserved rather than invented around, and a (cid:N) remap needs a per-font glyph table that the conversion path deliberately does not carry. NO EXPIRY: metadata.source_kind is 'native-digital', so nothing about the OCR decision touches it. If a future round finds a discriminator that separates a parenthesised SECTION from a parenthesised SUBSECTION without the contents page, delete this entry -- but measure it against those 2,505 lines first, and against the 83 in particular.

Three schedule leaves -- THE FIRST SCHEDULE, THE SECOND SCHEDULE and THE FIFTH SCHEDULE -- render with no <h4> at all, their html opening on the bracketed cross-reference instead ('[see section 4(29)]', '[See Section 4(30)]', '[see section 18(1A)]'). That is exactly the FS-01 shape fixed in this PR by removing the See-promotion branch in schedules._finish_leaf. metadata.source_kind is null and total_pages is 292. THE DOCUMENT'S OUTPUT PREDATES PROVENANCE STAMPING AND CANNOT BE RE-MEASURED. metadata.pipeline_revision and metadata.converted_at are both null -- this is one of the 14 acts documents every re-conversion since round 27 has skipped, because convert_all.scan_page_count reports it as scanned and re-converting it would run OCR, and data/ocr_cache must stay at 0 B under the decision of record (2026-09-04). Its output was therefore written by a parser many rounds older than this tree. BE CLEAR WHAT THIS ENTRY CLAIMS: the fix that closed this class shipped in this same PR and closed every LIVE instance of it in the corpus, so this hit is almost certainly nothing but stale-revision drift. That cannot be demonstrated, because the only way to demonstrate it is the re-conversion the OCR decision forbids. The entry exists because 'tracked and deferred' is not a state this suite allows. EXPIRY: the OCR decision. The day OCR is taken in scope, re-convert this document and delete this entry -- the suite will say so itself if the hit clears.
